subject.title: fix: bind bun x exec approvals to the inner command like bunx

question: Should existing allow-always entries for the outer `bun` executable intentionally stop authorizing `bun x` invocations, requiring approval of the resolved inner command instead?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but the compatibility-versus-least-privilege upgrade behavior is a durable security policy choice that tests cannot make for maintainers.

options.title: Accept inner-command binding
options.body: Merge the parity fix and intentionally require direct `bun x` commands to match durable approvals only through their resolved inner executable.

options.title: Preserve outer-bun compatibility
options.body: Keep outer `bun` entries effective for `bun x`, accepting the broader trust target and abandoning `bunx` parity for existing approvals.

options.title: Pause for policy guidance
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define a migration or user-facing approval-transition policy for existing outer-bun entries.

recommendation.title: Accept inner-command binding
recommendation.body: Merge the parity fix and intentionally require direct `bun x` commands to match durable approvals only through their resolved inner executable.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged package-manager approval-binding invariant that this PR extends.
